findings.claim: A legal drag is silently refused when the card is released in the empty tableau space just below the target column instead of on top of its cards: the same move (10♥ from col 6 onto J♣ at the bottom of col 0) is accepted when released at y=600 (over the cards) but snaps back with Moves unchanged when released 10 pt or 20 pt below the column's last card, so the player is taught that a legal move is illegal.

repro: fresh install, launch
tap the Deal # pill (192,175); tap the field (200,268); tap Select All (213,316); type 1,0,0,0,4 on the number pad; tap Play (200,336) -> deal #10,004, Moves 0
press-drag the 10♥ at the bottom of column 6 (321,612) and release at (28,700) - 20 pt below column 0's last card, whose bottom edge is y=680: card snaps back, Moves stays 0
repeat releasing at (28,690) (10 pt below): snaps back, Moves stays 0
repeat releasing at (28,600), over the column's cards: accepted, Moves = 1

findings.note: The strip below a column belongs to no other drop target, so extending each column's drop frame down to the tableau's bottom is unambiguous. TESTCASES TC-2.3 currently documents this as expected ('a release below the column's last card lands outside its drop zone'); this finding argues the documented behaviour is itself the defect.

findings.claim: Touching or dragging a card that cannot move produces literally zero on-screen response - no lift, no highlight, no shake, no message - so a novice cannot tell 'this card is not movable' from 'the app did not register my touch'. Filmed at ~4 fps for the whole 3 s press-drag of a buried card: every frame is bit-identical to the pre-drag frame.

repro: fresh install, launch, tap New game (51,135) (observed on deal #904390, Moves 0 so nothing else on screen animates)
press-drag the buried card at column 0 index 2 (28,500) towards (200,500) with a 3.0 s press duration
capture host screenshots (xcrun simctl io ... screenshot) continuously through the gesture and diff them against the pre-gesture frame
same gesture on the column's BOTTOM card (28,642) does visibly move the card - so the rig does deliver the gesture

findings.note: Applies to a plain tap on a buried card too (Moves unchanged, nothing drawn). Careful with the fix: tap is the primary control, so any refusal cue must not fire on ordinary taps of cards that ARE movable but have no target.

findings.claim: In portrait, the live daily objectives HUD squeezes all three chips onto one 402pt line, so Silver and Gold are cut off ('🥈 · Win in 103 moves or…', '🥇 · For every suit, send i…'). A player chasing Gold cannot read what Gold requires while playing; the same labels render in full in landscape and in the demo bar, so this is purely a portrait layout choice.

repro: fresh install, launch
tap Daily
tap Play (Today card, deal #10,005)
read the dark objectives capsule under the toolbar

measurements.landscape_gold_shown: For every suit, send its King home before its Ace

findings.note: Same text wraps to 3 lines in the demo bar on the same screen width, so multi-line/wrapping in the HUD is demonstrably feasible.

findings.claim: Tapping a 'Show me how to win' pill while a daily attempt is in progress silently throws that attempt away — no confirmation, no warning. Observed: Moves 2 / Time 0:51 with the objectives HUD up, tap Daily → 🥉 Clear, and the board instantly resets to Moves 0 / Undo disabled with the demo bar up; there is no way back to the discarded attempt.

repro: fresh install, launch
tap Daily, tap Play (deal #10,005)
tap the bottom card of column 0 (K♠ smart-moves home) and the bottom card of column 7 -> Moves 2, Time 0:51, HUD visible, Undo enabled
tap Daily
tap the 🥉 Clear pill under 'Show me how to win:'
observe the board: Moves 0, Undo disabled, demo bar replaces the HUD

findings.note: Cheap safe fix is a confirmation ('This ends your current daily attempt') before showSolution() re-deals; do NOT restore the pre-demo attempt after the demo, that reopens the 'finish the app's line' hole.

findings.claim: While a demo runs and on its completion banner, the player's own header shows the demo's move count against a stopped clock — 'Moves 86 / Time 0:00' after the 86-move Clear line finishes — so the header reads as if the user played a perfect 86-move, zero-second game.

repro: fresh install, launch
tap Daily, tap 🥉 Clear
tap Start and let the line run to 86 / 86 (~22 s)
read the header: Moves 86, Time 0:00, Won 0

findings.note: Cheap fix: blank or dim the Moves/Time readout while demoing || demoDoneMessage != nil. Nothing is actually banked (verified Won 0, Wins empty, all daily records 0).

findings.claim: The Daily screen's month calendar renders only 5 of the 7 weekday letters — Thursday's 'T' and Saturday's 'S' are missing, leaving two blank column headers above real day cells. Cause: ForEach(["S","M","T","W","T","F","S"], id: \.self) in DailyView.swift:271 collapses the duplicate ids.

repro: cold launch
tap Daily
scroll the Daily sheet down to the month calendar
read the weekday header row above the day grid: 'S M T W _ F _'

findings.note: Reproduced on every visit to the Daily sheet (2 screenshots, plus the source cause). Fix: give the ForEach a positional id (e.g. Array(...).enumerated() / indices), not the string value.

findings.claim: The Auto-finish pill cycles Ask -> On -> Off, so on a finishable board the only route from the default 'Ask' to 'Off' passes through 'On' — and the single tap that lands on 'On' immediately runs the whole auto-finish cascade, ends the game and records the win. A settings control silently performs an irreversible game action with no confirmation and no undo.

repro: fresh launch (defaults Auto-play: On, Auto-finish: Ask)
tap 'Deal #' pill, enter 10169, tap Play
play the 28 moves listed in TESTCASES TC-8.4 fixture (bronze line prefix for deal #10169) until the board is finishable
the 'Ready to finish' prompt appears (Ask working as labelled); tap 'Not yet' — the gold Finish pill stays and the board is still playable
now try to switch Auto-finish to 'Off' so you can finish the deal by hand: tap the 'Auto-finish: Ask' pill ONCE
the pill reads 'Auto-finish: On' and the app instantly cascades all 42 remaining cards home, shows the win overlay and records the win — 'Off' was never reachable

findings.note: TRAP: the naive fix (stop calling maybeAutoFinish() from autoFinishMode.didSet) would also kill the intended 'flip Auto-finish to On to finish this board now' affordance, which is the app's only shortcut to a cascade once 'Not yet' has been tapped. Safer shapes: cycle Ask -> Off -> On so the destructive state is never a pass-through, or route a pass-through into On on an already-finishable board via the same 'Ready to finish' confirm instead of firing immediately.

findings.claim: In landscape the DISABLED Undo control in the left rail renders as a completely blank white capsule - neither the arrow.uturn.backward glyph nor the word 'Undo' is discernible at 3x - so the rail shows an unexplained featureless button between 'New game' and 'Replay'. The identical disabled state in the portrait toolbar still reads as a greyed-out 'Undo'.

repro: launch the app fresh (or any state with an empty undo stack - the stack is empty after every relaunch)
rotate the device to landscape (XCUIDevice.shared.orientation = .landscapeLeft)
look at the second pill of the left control rail, between 'New game' and 'Replay' (pt 127,102 with no HUD; pt 127,141 with the daily HUD)

findings.note: Still present on 6ee255b; the same defect was filed in the previous (archived) loop on 342e3c0 under this same id and is carried in BACKLOG.md as an open minor. Verified the pill is fine once enabled (after one move it reads with the arrow glyph + 'Undo'), and fine in portrait when disabled, so it is the landscape rail's .buttonStyle(.plain) + .opacity(0.4) combination, not a width problem - 'Undo' fits easily in 117pt.

findings.claim: In landscape the 'Play a deal' alert shows only ONE of its three actions: 'Random' and 'Cancel' are laid out below the visible alert area, behind the auto-raised number pad, with no scroll indicator and only a ~5pt sliver as a hint. Tapping outside does not dismiss, so the only visible exit from the modal is 'Play', which replaces the game in progress. In portrait the identical alert shows Play/Random/Cancel all at once.

repro: launch the app fresh
rotate the device to landscape (XCUIDevice.shared.orientation = .landscapeLeft)
tap the 'Deal #...' pill in the left rail (pt 127,232 with no HUD; pt 127,271 with the daily HUD)
observe the alert: title, message, prefilled field, number pad up, and 'Play' as the only visible button
tap anywhere outside the alert (e.g. pt 780,40 and pt 60,380) - the alert does not dismiss and the pad stays up
drag upward inside the alert body (pt 437,200 -> 437,60) - the action list scrolls and 'Cancel' appears in the same slot where 'Play' was

findings.note: A landscape power user simply cannot see 'Random', and any user who opens the alert by accident has no visible way out except the destructive 'Play'. The actions ARE reachable by an undiscoverable scroll gesture inside the alert, so it is confusion rather than a hard block. Contributing cause is app-side, not just system layout: the field is auto-focused so the number pad eats ~170pt of the 402pt landscape height before the alert is even laid out. Cheapest fixes: do not auto-focus the field in landscape, or drop to two actions (Play/Cancel) with Random moved next to the field.

findings.claim: The first Export (or Import) tap in an app process freezes the whole UI for 1.6-1.8 s with byte-identical frames and no spinner, disabled state, or any other acknowledgement, so the user gets no evidence their tap registered before the Files sheet finally slides up; a second use in the same process costs 0.9 s, so the cost is a per-process UIDocumentPicker warm-up that recurs after every cold launch.

repro: xcrun simctl terminate + launch (cold start; the stall recurs on every cold launch, not once per install)
tap the 'Daily' toolbar pill
scroll the Daily sheet to the BACKUP section at the bottom
tap 'Export' (or, on another cold launch, 'Import')

observe: the pill's press highlight shows for ~0.4 s, then the screen is byte-for-byte frozen for ~1.0-1.2 s with no spinner, then the Files sheet starts to slide up (first pixel change 1.61 s after touch for Export, 1.80 s for Import); fully settled ~3.2 s after touch

measurements.identical_frame_proof: film_exportcold2 frames 016 (t+0.88 s) and 021 (t+1.84 s) share md5 c9a62b8843814dd7f6fd691a2de77227
measurements.lane: uncontended perf lane, other simulators shut down

findings.note: Same id was filed in the previous (archived) loop against 342e3c0 and never fixed; re-measured here on 6ee255b and it still reproduces, now with the Import path measured too. The warm-vs-cold control (0.92 s vs 1.61 s in the SAME driver-attached session, alongside 0.76-1.43 s for every in-app sheet/redeal) rules out the XCUITest attachment as the cause: the cost is UIDocumentPicker's first presentation in the process, which the app cannot make fast — but it can show a spinner/disabled pill or pre-warm the picker off the main thread. Double-tapping during the stall was harmless in the archived pass (only one sheet presented). Everything else measured this round was fast: cold launch to painted board 0.90 s, auto-finish cascade 0.19 s/card with the win overlay 0.21 s after the last card, demo auto-advance 0.251-0.257 s/move (unchanged from the archive), idle CPU 0.0-0.9 %, no RSS growth over 22 New-game cycles, zero network bytes.

findings.claim: The app source contains zero accessibilityIdentifier (and zero explicit accessibilityLabel) modifiers — grep across ios/Causeway/Causeway/**/*.swift returns nothing. Every UI-test query must fall back to visible-label text (which breaks on copy changes and localization) and every card interaction must use raw device-point coordinates (cards in CardView expose no stable handle at all), because there is no way to address a specific tableau column, free cell, foundation slot, header stat value, or demo-bar control programmatically. This also degrades VoiceOver: cards, slots and the Moves/Time/Won stat values have no meaningful accessibility semantics.

repro: grep -rn 'accessibilityIdentifier\|accessibilityLabel' ios/Causeway/Causeway --include='*.swift'
observe: no matches

findings.note: Highest-value identifiers to add: (1) CardView — e.g. 'card.<suit><rank>' or per-slot 'tableau.<col>.<idx>'; (2) header stat values in ContentView.stat — 'stat.moves' / 'stat.time' / 'stat.won'; (3) demo bar pills and headline — 'demo.next/start/stop/done', 'demo.headline'; (4) toolbar pills — 'toolbar.deal', 'toolbar.daily', 'toolbar.undo'; (5) DailyView showPill tiers — 'daily.demo.bronze/silver/gold'. With (1)+(2) the two round-1 regression tests could drop all raw coordinates and their positional staticText reads, and the TC-2.6 test could assert board-shrink monotonicity directly from element frames.
